job.title: Workplace Safety Manager - Bel Group Central Hawke's Bay
job.description:
If you love being close to the action, connecting with people at every level, and playing an active role across the full spectrum of health safety and wellbeing initiatives, this senior leadership role offers the chance to get involved, make improvements, and see the results of your work every day.  Initiative, pragmatism and the ability and willingness to have courageous conversations will be crucial here.  

Bel Group is a privately owned dairy farming business with significant scale, managing extensive agricultural operations across multiple sites in Central Hawke's Bay.  Employing approximately 70 staff across nine farm units and more than 3,500 hectares of farmland in the Takapau area, the business has established a strong reputation for operational performance and long-term success.

This newly created role reports directly to the General Manager and offers the chance to take ownership of a critical business function while helping shape its future direction in workplace, health, safety and wellbeing.  This is not a role for someone who prefers to work from behind a desk.  This is a genuine partnership role, that will see you spending time on farm with operational teams to build credibility, identify critical risks, and provide practical, real-time health, safety and wellbeing advice and guidance.  Operating within a large-scale, high-risk and regulated environment, the scope is broad and varied and you can be guaranteed that no two days will be the same.  
  
Your core mandate will be to ensure legislative requirements and industry best practice standards are met, support robust risk and incident management processes, develop and build training and capability programmes, and drive continuous improvement across all areas of health, safety, and wellbeing.  You will bring a hearty combination of energy, maturity and resilience to challenge existing practices, drive positive behavioural change, and embed a culture where safety, wellbeing, and accountability are part of everyday decision-making.  
  
We are looking for a hands-on health and safety leader who thrives in complex operational environments and has the credibility to influence at every level of the business.  You must hold relevant health and safety qualifications, have working knowledge of NZ health and safety regulations and legislation, and ideally have gained experience from within a farming, agricultural or horticultural environment.  You may be in a current health, safety and wellbeing leadership role now and looking for a fresh change, or you could be on your way to the next step in your career.  Either way, it will be important that you are able to hit the ground running on-site in Central Hawke’s Bay.  For the right person, this a rare chance to leave a lasting mark on a growing organisation, shape the future of workplace safety, and make a genuine difference to the lives of those who work within it.  Remuneration will reflect your experience. Please apply directly through this portal, or for further information, call the team at Populous People for a confidential discussion on 068758446.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
If you are an experienced project manager with exposure and experience across construction-related or civil environments, then this is a great team to be joining. You may already be leading a team across a range of projects, or on the tools currently and looking to take a step up into the commercial side of a business.
  
Our client, Eric Wiig Ltd is a well-run, highly successful Hawke’s Bay business. We’ve loved recruiting and building this team over the years. They are a great crew, well-known and highly regarded for their expertise in painting and specialist coating services across commercial, industrial and residential projects. They have been operating for over 50 years and continue to build strong client relationships which reflects in their ongoing growth. This project manager role is key in them managing their workflows and further stepping up their service delivery levels.
  
As the project manager of their resin flooring, waterproofing and specialist coatings division, you will sit across a broad range of projects from initial site measure and quotation, right through to project completion and final client handover. You will be responsible for the day-to-day team management and running of each job to ensure work is delivered safely, efficiently and to a high standard.
  
You will also be responsible for ensuring projects are delivered profitably, scheduling and coordinating labour, ensuring all materials are on hand, overseeing the quality of work, monitoring progress and keep clients informed along the way. This is a varied and hands-on role that will keep you busy, and you will be well supported by the experience of a team of project managers around you.
  
To be successful here, you will be well known for your people management skills, be results driven and will likely have sat across project management in trades-related practices. Knowledge of resin flooring processes and products is not essential but would be highly regarded. You will need to enjoy working at pace and be able to manage many priorities and demands at any one time.
  
We are looking for someone with the ambition to become an expert in their field - someone prepared to immerse themselves in the industry and continually develop their knowledge of products, systems and emerging technologies. You will be a confident communicator, capable of representing the business professionally. You will know how to manage and get the best out of people, have sound technical ability, strong communication and organisational skills, and be professional in your approach.
  
If you are looking for a hands-on leadership role working with a great bunch of people, then please apply through this Seek portal or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Mechanical Design Engineer - Lotek
job.description:
This is an exciting time to join a world-leading wildlife tracking engineering, manufacturing and sales team. You will be based in Hawkes Bay New Zealand, whilst working closely with the Canadian parent company.
  
This is a very clever business - the hardware and material you will be working on enables wildlife of all shapes and sizes to be tracked across the globe.  Lotek specialises in manufacturing devices that track creatures spanning avian, freshwater, marine and terrestrial wildlife forever aiming to innovate with smaller, stronger lighter devices. Their Radio, Acoustic, Archival, GPS and Satellite instruments deployed on animals throughout the world provide insight to animal behaviour, and how and where they spend their lives.
  
This career opportunity places you at the heart of their technology offering.
  
The core of this role is to design and create prototypes, moving prototypes into manufacturing, and enhancing existing product design and offerings. You will work closely with the engineering, production, and product management teams to design and bring to market new products and to refine existing products. You will ensure their smooth transition to commercial production as well as refining and redeveloping existing devices. Throughout this process, you will create and maintain documentation for all new parts, components, and assemblies. You will provide technical direction and guidance to technical staff and assist with training and development initiatives. A continuous improvement mindset with a focus on higher quality and efficiency is essential.
  
This role is suited to a tertiary-qualified engineer, with a track record ideally in packaging design, prototyping and verification testing. You must be able to demonstrate experience in design and hands-on fabrication of light production jigs and fixtures. Ideally you will have expertise relating to small battery-powered electronic packaging including mouldings. Either way, you must understand and show competence in the behaviour of epoxies, fabrics, glues, silicones and 4-axis CNC machining.  Proficiency with SolidWorks is important and knowledge and expertise in materials a definite plus.
  
You would be a self-starter with the ability to show initiative and think outside the box. Our products are highly unique and often fall outside conventional industry norms, incorporating materials sourced from a wide range of applications.
  
If you have the expertise to step into this very special role then we would love to hear from you. This will allow you to balance your career development and the chance to work on a global technology offering whilst living in sunny Hawkes Bay where great schooling and great lifestyle is just a given.
Please apply through this Seek portal or phone the team at Populous for a confidential discussion to learn more. Telephone 06 875 8446.

job.title: Transport Dispatcher - $40 - $60/hour
job.description:
If you love the thought of keeping big wheels moving and you want to be part of a fast-moving, well-run privately owned transport business, then this is a great role for you to consider. Experience in dispatch and freight will be rewarded.
  
Our client are specialists in log transport, providing log cartage services to customers across the North Island. They are well established, have a great reputation and pride themselves on investing in quality machinery and people.
  
As their Transport Dispatcher, you will sit right in the heart of the business. You will be responsible for effectively coordinating the transportation of log loads from various locations, to ensure customer and company KPIs are met as well as ensuring maximum cartage capacity is reached for each truck. You’ll coordinate and manage the schedules of trucks ensuring pickup and delivery targets are met, maintain all logistics data via in house software, and monitor and report on daily dispatch. You’ll be good at building credibility with each of the drivers, ensuring they have all the information they need to be set up for each day. You’ll have your finger on the pulse and be ready to respond and find solutions to any interruptions or issues to the schedule. There is complexity that sits around the grading of logs, and destinations in which these can go to, so you’ll need to be able to quickly come up to speed with these standards.
  
There are lots of moving parts here and an environment where plans can change quickly, so you must be good prioritizing workloads and communicating openly and clearly with where things are at.
  
This role will be well suited to those experienced working in dispatch. Ideally you will come from a dispatch role within the logging transport industry, however we are open to considering candidates from other industries. You must be level headed, be known for your problem-solving skills and have the ability to think quick on your feet. You’ll have strong relationship skills and be able to build rapport quickly with the drivers. If you have your HT license, that will be a real bonus.
  
You must relate to the pace and customer centric focus of a privately held company where the owners are hands on and play an active part in the business. You’ll be confident navigating various software systems and driving efficiencies. You may be working in a logging, forestry or transport company currently and looking for that next challenge, or you may or you could be an experienced log truck driver looking to move into an office-based role.
  
This role will be well remunerated. If you have the required background, then please apply now through the Seek portal or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 to learn more.

job.title: Procurement & Commercial Specialist - for Water Hawkes Bay
job.description:
This is a crucial transition and set-up role. If you consider yourself at home in procurement planning, supplier and contract management and you enjoy stakeholder engagement and relationship management this will be a great new challenge. You will be responsible for establishing the procurement and commercial arrangements that are required for Water Hawke’s Bay to commence operations on Day 1.

Water Hawke’s Bay is a council-controlled organisation (CCO) jointly owned by Hastings District, Napier City and Central Hawke’s Bay district councils, established under the Government’s Local Water Done Well Reforms. WHB is governed by an independent and commercially accountable Board; this is a chance to join a high performing team determined to get this right for the region.

This transition team will ensure that Water Hawke’s Bay is ready to begin delivering drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater services from 1 July 2027 with a focus on providing safe and reliable water services for generations to come.  In this role, you will ensure the services are transferred to WHB with minimal disruption to customers and the communities. This is a fixed term role until June 2027.

This role will develop the organisation’s procurement framework, coordinate the transition of fleet, supplier and contract arrangements from participating councils, provide procurement advice across the establishment programme and establish office and related facilities for WHB. Building on existing council procurement practices wherever appropriate, the role will establish procurement processes that support a new regional water services organisation while reflecting good public sector procurement practice.

To succeed in this role, you will bring senior level procurement expertise.  Public sector procurement strategy, policy and process development, and end to end procurement and supplier management and commercial contract management are key experience sets required here. Experience working with procurement governance and delegated authority frameworks aligned to local government, infrastructure or regulated utility environments will be highly regarded and help ensure you hit the ground running here. 

If you have the required procurement expertise and can build credible and trusted commercial relationships quickly, we would love to hear from you. Remuneration will reflect the significance of this role. Please apply through this portal. Or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Supply Planner
job.description:
If you have experience in supply and demand planning, understand key ERP and supply planning principles, and enjoy the analysis and discipline that underpin effective planning, we'd love to hear from you.  Whether you're an emerging supply chain professional with three to four years' experience ready for the next step in your career, or an experienced planner looking for a role where your expertise is truly valued, this is an opportunity worth exploring.
We genuinely enjoy partnering with this client and have seen many people thrive, grow, and build rewarding careers within the business over the years.  They are a successful, growth-focused manufacturer and exporter based in Hawke's Bay, where strong supply chain planning plays a critical role in their ongoing success.

Reporting to a highly capable and forward-thinking S&OP Planning Manager, this role offers the chance to make a meaningful impact on the planning function.  As supply planner, you will be responsible for ensuring the right products are available at the right time while balancing inventory, production, and cost considerations.  Your day-to-day responsibilities will include forecasting demand, developing production plans, managing inventory levels, and coordinating with suppliers to secure ingredients and packaging. You'll work closely with manufacturing, procurement, warehousing, and 3PL partners to ensure products are stored, transported, and distributed efficiently.  In time, you'll become a key link between production inputs and outputs, helping to shape planning decisions across both the short and long-term horizon.

You may hold a qualification in supply chain management, although practical experience and a sound understanding of end-to-end supply chain planning processes are equally important.  Strong organisational and communication skills are essential, along with the ability to build effective relationships with internal stakeholders and external suppliers.  A naturally curious mindset, strong problem-solving ability, and a proactive approach will see you succeed in this role.  You'll also bring excellent administration and Excel skills, along with the confidence to learn new systems quickly.  In return, you'll be joining a supportive and high-performing team that genuinely values the contribution of its people.  If you have the required expertise, please apply through this portal or telephone Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Group Financial Controller
job.description:
An Internal promotion and clear growth trajectory with key global customers mean this finance leadership role provides an excellent career opportunity for a rising finance leader. This Gisborne-based Group Financial Controller role will be well suited to a commercially savvy, growth focused finance leader.

Corson is a family owned 100-year legacy business that has long been recognised for producing high-quality maize for food ingredients.

They were founded and continue to be grounded in Gisborne, but from there they reach far. They have real market strength, with operations in both NZ and Australia. Their close relationships with major FMCG customers see their finished product sitting as the base of many household food brands across Australasia.

Over the last 3 years the business has been in a recovery and reinvestment phase. They have invested in a new mill which is due to be commissioned later this year and implemented new accounting systems and process across the group focused on a digital future; so this is a great time to be joining the business.

As Group Financial Controller, you will provide the commercial and finance leadership to help steer them through their next phase of growth. You will lead the key aspects of financial management, reporting, compliance, cash flow management, risk and financial planning across the New Zealand and Australia operations. You will engage with operational leaders across the business to support business performance and profitability through providing meaningful financial insights and recommendations. This is a hands-on role, leading a small transactional finance and customer service team where you will oversee budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis for the group – ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting for the board and shareholders.

To be considered, you must be CA or CPA qualified with a strong knowledge of IFRS financial reporting standards, taxation and compliance. As well as proficiency in management accounting principles including pricing, revenue analysis and inventory cost analysis. Along with your strong technical expertise, you will need a big-picture mentality, be commercially astute and be comfortable challenging the status quo. An understanding of the complexities of manufacturing-based environments will be a real advantage here.
You may already be in a finance leadership role, or at the point in your career where a step up to a role like this is your next career challenge. There is a genuine pathway here for the right person.

Roles of this commercial nature are rare in Gisborne, you will be joining a great team with a huge commitment to growth and development. If you have the required finance expertise, people leadership experience and commercial strategic capacity to perform here, then please apply through this portal. Or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Finance roles - two influential opportunities
job.description:
This is a great opportunity to be part of the Water Hawke's Bay (WHB) establishment team – your input and engagement stands to make a lasting contribution in terms of how water services and infrastructure is set up and managed across the Hawke’s Bay region moving forward. Best practice finance clarity and systems will sit at the heart of these roles.

We are recruiting two different roles, reporting to the Finance, Funding and Commercial Lead.  
  • Financial Planning Specialist
  • Revenue, Charging & Billing Specialist,
Both of these roles are fixed term until June 2027 and will play a key part in establishing the finance systems and best practice for a new era for water services across Hawke’s Bay.

Water Hawke’s Bay is a council-controlled organisation (CCO) jointly owned by Hastings District, Napier City and Central Hawke’s Bay district councils, established under the Government’s Local Water Done Well Reforms. WHB is governed by an independent and commercially accountable Board.
The establishment team will ensure that Water Hawke’s Bay is ready to begin delivering drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater services from 1 July 2027 with a focus on providing safe and reliable water services for generations to come. This is your chance to have a real impact on this region’s future – you will be joining a high performing, focused team who are determined to get this right for Hawke’s Bay.

As Financial Planning Specialist, you will be responsible for establishing the financial planning and business planning capability required to support Water Hawke’s Bay through transition and into Day 1 operations. This is a finance business partnering role with a strong management accounting focus. You will coordinate and scrutinise financial information from participating councils and integrate specialist modelling advice into practical planning, budgeting, forecasting and decision making. To be considered, you will ideally be CA or CPA qualified with a strong knowledge of financial planning, analysis, forecasting and driving operational budgets. You will feel at home working alongside financial modelling advisors to develop and implement the WHB’s financial forecasting model, all with a view to supporting strategic decision making. You’ll have strong stakeholder relationship skills, be commercially minded and be able to challenge council models, data and frameworks.

The Revenue, Charging & Billing Specialist will be responsible for designing and implementing the revenue and customer charging framework required for WHB to commence operations on Day 1. This includes determining the water rates, ensuring sufficient income to cover maintenance costs, as well as funding growth for the future. This will be suited to those with an economics and commercial lens, ideally with infrastructure and asset exposure. Those with experience within NZ local government funding, utility charging, rating or revenue management will be highly regarded for this specific role.

Both of these roles will be suited to those who want to take an early lead in shaping the finance planning and revenue structures of Water Hawke's Bay. 

If you have the required finance expertise, strategic capacity and stakeholder engagement ability to perform here, then please apply through this portal. Or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more of what this could mean for your career. Competitive market rates and remuneration reflect the significance of these two roles.
